summary: Describes the interface between the Mail Transfer Protocol software and the NIMAIL mail system in the ISI TOPS-20 implementation. It is a companion to the main implementation description.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 786 defines how MTP and NIMAIL exchange mail through files on ISI TOPS-20. It specifies the file form and how addresses are translated in each direction.

questions: how does mtp send mail to nimail
how do mtp and nimail exchange mail
subtitle: The file interface between MTP and NIMAIL on ISI TOPS-20.

tldr.problem: The MTP and NIMAIL mail systems on ISI TOPS-20 need defined files and address transformations to exchange messages.
tldr.mechanism: NIMAIL presents files in the RFC 785 format; MTP presents a recipient list, Via line, headers, and body in files placed in the NIMAIL directory.
tldr.outcome: The memo specifies the bidirectional file interface and shows how each system transforms the other's address format.

today: RFC 786 specifies a file interface between MTP and NIMAIL on ISI TOPS-20. It relies on the file formats defined in the referenced MTP documents.

sections.title: A File-Based Mail Interface
sections.content:
The memo defines the interface between the Mail Transfer Protocol and Network Independent Mail on ISI TOPS-20 in terms of the files each system uses. NIMAIL gives MTP files in the format defined by RFC 785.

MTP gives NIMAIL files with destination addresses, a Via line, headers, and a body.
sections.plainLanguage: The two mail systems pass messages by placing files in the format expected by the other system. This memo defines those file forms for ISI TOPS-20.

sections.title: Mail from MTP to NIMAIL
sections.content:
An MTP-to-NIMAIL file starts with one or more recipient addresses, followed by a blank line and a Via line containing the sending host and date-time. The message headers and body follow.

Addresses in one file must share the same final @host part. The file name ends in .NIMAIL.-1 and the file is placed in the NIMAIL directory.
sections.plainLanguage: The file begins with its recipients and routing information, then contains the message. Recipients in one file share the same final host part.

sections.title: Converting Address Formats
sections.content:
When NIMAIL sends joe%hostx%hosty%hostz@isie to MTP, the interface represents the sender as NIMAIL at ISIE and converts the destination into an MTP route.

In the reverse direction, the MTP address <@ISIE,@hostz,@hosty,joe@hostx> is converted to a NIMAIL percent-routed address and a Via line identifying ISIE.
sections.plainLanguage: NIMAIL and MTP write routed addresses differently. Each side converts the address when it prepares the file for the other system.
